title: Power-bounded elements are integral over a presentation unit ball
statement: Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean field with a nontrivial rank-one absolute value and valuation ring $V=\{a\in K:|a|\leq1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Let $q:K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle\to C$ be a continuous surjective homomorphism onto a nonzero affinoid $K$-algebra, where the Tate algebra consists of power series with coefficients tending to zero and $C$ has its affinoid Banach topology. Put $D=q(V\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle)$, where the restricted series in $V\langle T\rangle$ have coefficients in $V$. If $c\in C$ has bounded powers $\{c^m:m\geq0\}$, then $c$ satisfies a monic polynomial of positive degree with coefficients in $D$. No reducedness or algebraic closedness is assumed.

source.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, printed pp. 28-29, and Proposition 4(iii), printed p. 23 (the quotient-norm infimum is attained); primary PDF read online, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affinoid-quotient-norm-topology] to the given presentation $q$. Its quotient Gauss norm $\|\cdot\|_q$ is equivalent to the affinoid Banach norm, so the hypothesis on powers gives a real $M\ge1$ with $\|c^m\|_q\le M$ for all $m\ge0$. Write $\rho_C$ for the maximal-ideal supremum of [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus].

source.place: Section 1.4, Proposition 4(i)-(ii), Proposition 19 alternative proof, and Theorem 16(iii).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus], $\rho_C(c)^m=\rho_C(c^m)\le\|c^m\|_q\le M$ for every $m\ge1$. If $\rho_C(c)=1+\delta$ with $\delta>0$, the binomial expansion gives $\rho_C(c)^m\ge1+m\delta$; choosing an integer $m>(M-1)/\delta$ contradicts the bound. Therefore $\rho_C(c)\le1$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, implication (iii) to (i), using Propositions 5 and 8.

proof.text: The ideal $I=\ker q$ is proper since $q(1)=1\ne0$. Apply [lem-trf-tate-normalization-lift] to get an injection $\iota:B=K\langle U_1,\ldots,U_d\rangle\to K\langle T_1,\ldots,T_r\rangle$ for which $\varphi=q\iota:B\to C$ is injective and finite. Here $K\langle T\rangle/I\cong C$ by $f+I\mapsto q(f)$, so the finite generating set given by normalization maps to a finite $B$-module generating set of $C$.

source.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, normalization step; Section 1.2, Corollary 10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-affinoid-spectral-equation] to $\varphi:B\to C$ and $c$. This gives $n\ge1$, $b_i\in B$, and $c^n+\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi(b_i)c^{n-i}=0$ with $\max_i\rho_B(b_i)^{1/i}=\rho_C(c)\le1$. Thus each $\rho_B(b_i)\le1$. Both algebras are nonzero affinoids and $\varphi$ is finite by step 3; no torsion-free or reducedness hypothesis is needed for this cited statement.

source.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, implication (i) to (ii), using Lemma 13.

proof.text: For each $i$, [lem-trf-affinoid-supremum-seminorm-calculus] gives $\|\iota(b_i)\|_G=\rho_{K\langle T\rangle}(\iota(b_i))\le\rho_B(b_i)\le1$. Every coefficient of the restricted series $\iota(b_i)$ therefore has absolute value at most one, so $\iota(b_i)\in V\langle T\rangle$ and $a_i=q(\iota(b_i))=\varphi(b_i)\in D$. The monic polynomial $X^n+\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX^{n-i}\in D[X]$ has positive degree and vanishes at $c$ by step 4. This uses the original $q$, without changing its unit ball.

source.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, final coefficient estimate from Propositions 6 and 7.

proof_origin.place: Section 1.4, Theorem 16, printed pp.28-29. Reconstruction of its (iii) to (i) to (ii) argument from primary PDF read online; archival copy WANTED. Norm-topology input uses the open mapping alternative to Proposition 19 to avoid circular use of Theorem 16.

lean.statement: theorem affinoid_powerbounded_integral (K : Type u) [NontriviallyNormedField K] [IsUltrametricDist K] [CompleteSpace K] (V : ValuationSubring K) (hV : ∀ a : K, a ∈ V ↔ ‖a‖ ≤ 1) (r : ℕ) (C : Type v) [NormedCommRing C] [Nontrivial C] [NormedAlgebra K C] [IsUltrametricDist C] [CompleteSpace C] (q : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))) →+* C) (hscalar : q.comp (constants K r) = algebraMap K C) (hsurj : Function.Surjective q) (hcont : ∀ s, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ t, MvPowerSeries.gaussNorm (norm : K → ℝ) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ 1) (t.val - s.val) < δ → ‖q t - q s‖ < ε) (c : C) (hbounded : ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ m : ℕ, ‖c ^ m‖ ≤ M) : ∃ p : Polynomial C, p.Monic ∧ 0 < p.natDegree ∧ p.eval c = 0 ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, ∃ s : (MvPowerSeries.IsRestricted.subring (R := K) (fun _ : Fin r ↦ (1 : ℝ))), (∀ ν : Fin r →₀ ℕ, MvPowerSeries.coeff ν s.val ∈ V) ∧ q s = p.coeff i

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause: K is a complete ultrametric NontriviallyNormedField; V is pinned to the unit ball by hV (ValuationSubring, the def-trf-valuation-ring notion); the Tate algebra is Mathlib IsRestricted.subring at polyradius 1 with the recorded RestrictedSeries.constants; C is a nonzero complete ultrametric NormedAlgebra with q continuous for the Gauss norm, surjective and scalar-compatible, the same encoding as the landed AffinoidQuotientNormTopology; by the open mapping theorem this is exactly the affinoid topology, with no stronger assumption. Conclusion: monic p in C[X] of positive degree vanishing at c, each coefficient lifting through q to a series with coefficients in V, equivalent to a polynomial over D=q(V<T>). Edge cases r=0, c=0/1, nilpotent of large norm in K<T>/(T^2), idempotent in KxK, C=0 excluded.
